title: Markets: Thursday 22 October

morning.session_note: Weekday ASX edition · before the 10:00 open
summary: Wall Street rose on Wednesday: the S&P 500 gained 0.6% to 7,757.2 and the Nasdaq 1.1%, led by SpaceX and Super Micro results. After the bell, Meta and Tesla both beat LSEG revenue estimates and rose in extended trading. Brent futures settled 3 cents higher at US$108.82, and early reports had ASX 200 futures little changed ([AP via WAtoday](https://www.watoday.com.au/business/markets/asx-set-for-flat-start-wall-street-climbs-meta-ordered-to-pay-36-billion-in-privacy-case-tesla-results-ahead-20261022-p617mw.html), [Reuters via Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/oil-rises-middle-east-supply-005041638.html), [AFR](https://www.afr.com/markets/equity-markets/asx-steady-nasdaq-surges-meta-to-report-20261022-p617mq)).

For Australia, ASX futures put the chance of a 3 November RBA hike at 51% at Wednesday's close, up from 22% on Tuesday, after Deputy Governor Hauser said the inflation outlook was "materially worse". Goldman Sachs now expects a hike, while CBA's chief economist warned a hike could push the economy "over the edge" ([RBA Watch](https://rbawatch.com/rba-meeting/november-2026), [Reuters via Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/australia-central-banker-says-policy-221416518.html), [Brisbane Times](https://www.brisbanetimes.com.au/politics/federal/reserve-bank-in-nightmare-position-as-it-considers-another-rate-cut-in-november-20261021-p617c9.html)).

Next: New Zealand CPI at 8:45am, BHP's AGM at 10am, Fortescue and Santos quarterlies, and the Bank of Korea decision today; then Australia's annual national accounts and Zip's quarterly update on Friday, and Moody's scheduled review of France late Friday European time ([Stats NZ](https://www.stats.govt.nz/release-calendar/), [BHP](https://www.bhp.com/investor-centre/shareholder-information/annual-general-meetings), [Westpac Weekly](https://library.westpaciq.com.au/content/dam/public/westpaciq/secure/economics/documents/aus/2026/10/WestpacWeekly20261019.pdf)).

cards.headline: Nasdaq rose 1.1% as SpaceX and Super Micro lifted AI stocks
cards.takeaway: Technology was the best-performing sector and chipmakers rallied; communication services fell as Netflix and AT&T dropped after their results.
cards.new_since_last_issue: The previous issue covered SpaceX's after-hours result. Wednesday was the first full session after it, and Super Micro's revenue update and Netflix's regular-session fall are new.
cards.what_happened: The S&P 500 rose 44.60 points to 7,757.17, within 0.8% of the record it set earlier this month, the Dow rose 360.21 points (0.7%) to 52,856.09 and the Nasdaq rose 278.04 points to 26,702.86. SpaceX shares rose 7.8% after its first profit as a listed company, and Elon Musk said a merger of SpaceX and Tesla would be "a good idea" ([Reuters via MarketScreener](https://ca.marketscreener.com/news/nasdaq-leads-wall-street-to-higher-close-as-spacex-super-micro-boost-ai-sentiment-ce785cd9dd8cf725)); Super Micro rose 9.5% after saying it expects stronger revenue than it had forecast because of "increased demand for AI platforms", and Nvidia rose 2.5%. Netflix fell 5.3% after a fourth-quarter revenue forecast below expectations, and AT&T fell 6.4% after an earnings forecast that fell short of some analysts' expectations ([AP via WAtoday](https://www.watoday.com.au/business/markets/asx-set-for-flat-start-wall-street-climbs-meta-ordered-to-pay-36-billion-in-privacy-case-tesla-results-ahead-20261022-p617mw.html)). Technology was the best-performing of the 11 S&P 500 sectors, chipmakers rallied after an eight-session sell-off earlier this month, and Abbott fell after cutting its 2026 sales growth forecast ([Reuters via MarketScreener](https://ca.marketscreener.com/news/nasdaq-leads-wall-street-to-higher-close-as-spacex-super-micro-boost-ai-sentiment-ce785cd9dd8cf725)).
cards.why_it_matters: AI-linked shares sold off last week, with data-centre operator CoreWeave at the centre, and the reports "appeared to provide some reassurance" to investors worried about the sustainability of AI spending ([Reuters via MarketScreener](https://ca.marketscreener.com/news/nasdaq-leads-wall-street-to-higher-close-as-spacex-super-micro-boost-ai-sentiment-ce785cd9dd8cf725)). Locally, NextDC fell 42% on Wednesday after cutting its FY27 guidance, as covered on the Close tab ([ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-10-21/asx-markets-business-live-news-oct-22-2026/107290728)).
cards.market_reaction: Dashboard: S&P 500 +0.6% to 7,757.2, Nasdaq +1.1% to 26,702.9 and VIX down 0.63 points to 16.68 (21 Oct close, delayed). ASX 200 8,831.3, +0.2% (21 Oct close). ASX SPI futures are not in our data feed.

competing_views.view: The SpaceX and Super Micro results will not "answer all the questions investors have on returns on AI investments, but it's a good start."
The reaction was "a reaffirmation that the artificial intelligence trade is still intact", but sentiment can shift quickly and investors will look to Meta's results for confirmation.

cards.what_to_watch: Thursday US time (Friday morning in Sydney) brings results from Procter & Gamble, Newmont, Blackstone, American Airlines and Union Pacific; Alphabet and Microsoft report next Wednesday US time.

cards.headline: Meta beat revenue forecasts; capex exceeded operating cash flow
cards.takeaway: Revenue rose 26% and fourth-quarter guidance was above estimates, but a US$9.89 billion legal charge cut profit and free cash flow was negative.
cards.key_figure: Q3 revenue US$64.60bn vs US$63.37bn expected (LSEG, via CNBC)
cards.what_happened: Meta reported third-quarter revenue of US$64.60 billion, up 26%, and diluted earnings per share of US$3.83. Costs included a US$9.89 billion charge for its August agreement with 52 state attorneys general over teen mental health litigation; excluding it, EPS would have been US$7.40. Capital expenditure, including finance-lease principal, was US$34.91 billion against operating cash flow of US$32.79 billion, so free cash flow was negative US$2.12 billion. Meta guided to fourth-quarter revenue of US$73–76 billion, narrowed its 2026 capex range to US$135–145 billion from US$130–145 billion, and announced a new non-voting Class C share, to be distributed as a one-for-one stock dividend after it takes effect on 19 January 2027 ([Meta](https://investor.atmeta.com/investor-news/press-release-details/2026/Meta-Reports-Third-Quarter-2026-Results/default.aspx)). The fourth-quarter midpoint was above the US$73.73 billion analysts expected, and daily active people of 3.64 billion were below the 3.65 billion StreetAccount expected ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/21/meta-earnings-q3-2026-live-updates.html)). Earlier on Wednesday a New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay US$25 billion in a consumer protection case ([AP via WAtoday](https://www.watoday.com.au/business/markets/asx-set-for-flat-start-wall-street-climbs-meta-ordered-to-pay-36-billion-in-privacy-case-tesla-results-ahead-20261022-p617mw.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: Meta reported ahead of Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon; the four companies have called for roughly US$730 billion of capital expenditure this year, and analysts polled by FactSet expect about US$1 trillion next year, according to CNBC. That spending drives demand for AI chips, power and data-centre capacity.
cards.market_reaction: Meta shares rose 7% after the results, according to Investing.com (story updated 4:48pm New York time); they had closed up 0.46% in the regular session.

competing_views.view: Expected an in-line quarter and said a capex increase "could be received more positively (or less negatively)" now that Meta is "demonstrating a clearer ROI".

competing_views.who: Bank of America analysts (before the result)
competing_views.view: Expect the Muse AI assistant to "consume capacity w/o near-term revs" through this year and 2027.

comparison.title: Did Meta beat on earnings per share?
comparison.why_different: The estimates were compiled on different bases. Meta's reported EPS of US$3.83 includes the US$9.89 billion legal charge; US$7.40 excludes it. According to CNBC, it was not clear whether the result was comparable with LSEG's US$5.75 estimate; Investing.com compared it with a US$3.57 consensus. Neither outlet says whether its estimate includes the charge, so which estimate is like-for-like is unresolved. The figures should not be averaged.

rows.measure: Diluted EPS, GAAP and excluding the charge

cards.what_to_watch: Alphabet and Microsoft report next Wednesday US time, and Amazon on Thursday US time (29 and 30 October in Sydney).

cards.headline: Tesla's revenue topped LSEG estimates as auto sales fell 3%
cards.takeaway: Adjusted EPS beat, profit fell 29% on AI and robotics spending, and free cash flow turned positive; reported capex figures differ between outlets.
cards.key_figure: Q3 revenue US$28.05bn vs US$27.9bn expected (LSEG, via CNBC)
cards.new_since_last_issue: The previous issue listed Tesla as due; the results are new. Musk's merger comments were made on SpaceX's call on Tuesday.
cards.what_happened: Tesla reported revenue of US$28.05 billion and adjusted EPS of 48 cents, against LSEG estimates of US$27.9 billion and 43 cents. Automotive revenue fell 3% to US$20.56 billion and energy revenue fell 16% to US$2.88 billion. Net income fell 29% to US$787 million, and free cash flow was US$1.53 billion, after a negative second quarter ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/21/tesla-tsla-q3-2026-earnings-report.html)). Revenue was below the Bloomberg consensus of US$28.13 billion. Tesla said Optimus robot production had started at Fremont, and it has guided to more than US$25 billion of capex in 2026 ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/tesla-reports-q3-earnings-beat-free-cash-flow-and-capex-better-than-expected-200715033.html)). On SpaceX's call on Tuesday, Musk said both companies' boards had formed special committees to discuss a possible combination and that a Tesla vote would need 50% of all shares, "quite a high hurdle" ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/21/tesla-tsla-q3-2026-earnings-report.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: Tesla's results are a read on electric-vehicle demand and on spending for AI and robotics. Tesla said its vehicle sales in Australia, Canada, Japan and Taiwan reached records in the quarter ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/21/tesla-tsla-q3-2026-earnings-report.html)). Whether it beat or missed on revenue depends on which consensus is used (see figures).
cards.market_reaction: Tesla shares rose more than 1% in extended trading after a 3.4% gain in the regular session ([AP via WAtoday](https://www.watoday.com.au/business/markets/asx-set-for-flat-start-wall-street-climbs-meta-ordered-to-pay-36-billion-in-privacy-case-tesla-results-ahead-20261022-p617mw.html)).

comparison.title: How much did Tesla spend on capex?
comparison.why_different: Two outlets report different capital expenditure for the same quarter, and both say free cash flow was US$1.53 billion. We could not open Tesla's update deck in this run to check which figure it gives, so this is unresolved. Separately, revenue consensus differs by provider (LSEG US$27.9 billion, Bloomberg US$28.13 billion), which is why one outlet calls revenue a beat and the other a miss.

rows.measure: Q3 capital expenditure ("more than doubled" from a year earlier)

cards.what_to_watch: Tesla's responses to the US safety regulator's special order on the Cybercab are due on 30 October, according to Yahoo Finance.

cards.headline: Brent settled flat after a US$2 swing; US crude stocks fell
cards.takeaway: Prices rose early on Iranian statements and tanker attacks, then gave the gains back; EIA data showed a bigger crude draw than forecast and a surprise rise in distillates.
cards.key_figure: Brent futures settled at US$108.82, +0.03% (21 Oct, Reuters)
cards.new_since_last_issue: Tuesday's reversal from a five-month high was covered in the previous issue. New are Wednesday's intraday rise above US$110, the EIA inventory data and the US heating oil reserve offer.
cards.what_happened: Brent futures settled 3 cents higher at US$108.82 a barrel and WTI fell 67 cents to US$97.15, after both had gained more than US$2 during the session. US crude stocks fell 3.06 million barrels to 412.5 million in the latest week, against a Reuters poll forecast of an 820,000-barrel draw, while distillate stocks rose 1.68 million barrels against an expected 1.16 million-barrel fall, the EIA said. The Department of Energy offered to loan up to nearly a third of the 1-million-barrel emergency heating oil reserve. Kpler recorded at least 18 vessel attacks over two weeks ([Reuters via Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/oil-rises-middle-east-supply-005041638.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: The RBA's August forecasts assumed oil near US$80 a barrel ([Brisbane Times](https://www.brisbanetimes.com.au/politics/federal/reserve-bank-in-nightmare-position-as-it-considers-another-rate-cut-in-november-20261021-p617c9.html)), and Hauser cited oil as part of the reason the inflation outlook is worse (see Rates & expectations). Santos and Karoon report quarterly production today.
cards.market_reaction: Dashboard: Brent futures US$109.75, +0.9% (Yahoo BZ=F last trade at 7:23am AEDT, delayed); the EIA Brent spot series is unavailable before the cutoff. Gold futures +0.2% to US$4,152.2. Iron ore prices are not in our data feed.

competing_views.view: Crude was "trading both sides of unchanged" and "well below the overnight highs as attacks in the Strait of Hormuz look to be continuing".

cards.headline: CSL named GSK's Deborah Waterhouse as chief executive
cards.takeaway: She starts on 1 February 2027 and will stay based in the UK; interim CEO Gordon Naylor returns to the board.
cards.key_figure: Base salary £1.5 million; start date 1 Feb 2027
cards.new_since_last_issue: Lodged with the ASX at 4:37pm AEDT on Wednesday, after the close; CSL's Close-tab note said there was no new announcement at the time.
cards.what_happened: CSL appointed Deborah Waterhouse, chief executive of ViiV Healthcare and president of GSK Global Health, as CEO and managing director from 1 February 2027, after a global search. The board's decision was unanimous. Waterhouse will retain her base in the UK and spend significant time in Australia, the US and CSL's major markets; Gordon Naylor stays as interim CEO until then. Her contract has a £1.5 million base salary, short-term incentives of 120% of salary at target and long-term incentives of 250% at target, plus a £7.71 million award to replace forfeited GSK awards. She is restricted from involvement in CSL's Seqirus vaccines business until 31 March 2027 because of her previous role ([CSL](https://newsroom.csl.com/2026-10-21-CSL-appoints-Deborah-Waterhouse-as-CEO-Managing-Director), [AFR](https://www.afr.com/companies/healthcare-and-fitness/csl-names-british-pharma-executive-as-new-ceo-20261021-p617km)).
cards.why_it_matters: CSL has had an interim chief executive while the board searched. Chair Brian McNamee said in February the next CEO would need to "renew our pipeline and simplify our operations"; the ASX marked the announcement price-sensitive ([ASX announcements feed](https://asx.api.markitdigital.com/asx-research/1.0/companies/CSL/announcements)).
cards.market_reaction: Not yet traded; CSL closed at A$196.08, −0.1%, on Wednesday before the announcement (snapshot).
cards.what_to_watch: The first trading reaction from 10am, and CSL's AGM later this season.

cards.headline: Fortescue and Santos report; BHP holds its AGM at 10am
cards.takeaway: Fortescue's full quarterly follows its 8 October preliminary update, which flagged sales below shipments because of talks with China's state iron ore buyer.
cards.what_happened: Fortescue, Santos and Karoon Energy are due to release quarterly updates today, and AGMs include BHP, Brambles, IAG, ASX, APA Group, Cleanaway and Aurizon ([CommSec](https://www.commsec.com.au/content/dam/EN/ResearchNews/2026Reports/October/ECO_Insights_161026-Week-Ahead.pdf)). BHP's AGM starts at 10am Sydney time at Sydney Showground ([BHP](https://www.bhp.com/investor-centre/shareholder-information/annual-general-meetings)). In its preliminary update, Fortescue said September-quarter shipments were 46.8 million tonnes, 6% lower than a year earlier, sales of 42.9 million tonnes were below shipments "reflecting impacts from ongoing negotiations with China Mineral Resources Group", and net debt rose to US$2.8 billion; FY27 guidance was unchanged, subject to those negotiations ([Fortescue](https://content.fortescue.com/fortescue17114-fortescueeb60-productionbbdb-8be5/media/project/fortescueportal/shared/documents/regulatory/asx-announcements/automated/03145859-september-2026-quarterly-performance-update.pdf)). As of 7:40am AEDT, neither Fortescue nor Santos had lodged today's report ([ASX announcements feed](https://asx.api.markitdigital.com/asx-research/1.0/companies/FMG/announcements)).
cards.why_it_matters: Fortescue's report is the first full update since the preliminary figures and may say more about the China Mineral Resources Group talks, which affect sales volumes. Santos reports with Brent futures near US$109.
cards.what_to_watch: The quarterlies through the day; Zip, Mineral Resources and Whitehaven Coal report on Friday.

cards.headline: RBA November hike odds rose to 51% at Wednesday's close
cards.takeaway: Futures odds rose from 22% after Hauser's comments; Goldman now expects a hike, and CBA and Betashares economists warn of recession risk.
cards.key_figure: RBA cash rate 4.60% (last move +25 bp, 30 Sep)
cards.new_since_last_issue: Hauser's remarks were covered on Wednesday's Close tab. New are the closing futures reading and economists' responses.
cards.what_happened: ASX 30-day interbank futures implied a 51% chance of a 25 bp hike on 3 November at Wednesday's close, up from 22% on Tuesday, and prediction markets had 56% ([RBA Watch](https://rbawatch.com/rba-meeting/november-2026)). Hauser said the inflation outlook "does look materially worse" than in August, partly because of oil, and described the board's choice as whether to "do more to tackle high inflation" or "hold our horses to protect the labour market". Unemployment rose to 4.7% in September ([Reuters via Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/australia-central-banker-says-policy-221416518.html)). Treasurer Jim Chalmers said the war in the Middle East has been "pushing up inflation around the world, and in Australia" ([Brisbane Times](https://www.brisbanetimes.com.au/politics/federal/reserve-bank-in-nightmare-position-as-it-considers-another-rate-cut-in-november-20261021-p617c9.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: A hike would take the cash rate to 4.85%, raising repayments for variable-rate borrowers. September-quarter CPI on 28 October could show headline inflation at 4.0% with core around 3.5%, according to Reuters, above the RBA's 2–3% target band.
cards.market_reaction: Dashboard: AUD/USD 0.7010, +0.37% (RBA, 4pm 21 Oct); outlets reported it stronger overnight ([AP via WAtoday](https://www.watoday.com.au/business/markets/asx-set-for-flat-start-wall-street-climbs-meta-ordered-to-pay-36-billion-in-privacy-case-tesla-results-ahead-20261022-p617mw.html)), but our dashboard shows only the RBA's 4pm rate. AU 2Y 4.92% and AU 10Y 5.31% are from 14 Oct (RBA, published with a lag) and do not reflect this week.

competing_views.view: Absent a downside surprise in September-quarter CPI, the remarks "make a further hike in November more likely than not".
Warned the RBA could push the economy "over the edge" if it lifted rates to 4.85% in November.
"The RBA seems increasingly prepared to risk a recession to get inflation down."

cards.what_to_watch: RBA research paper on forecasters' perceived policy rules at 2:30pm today; Assistant Governor Hunter on 60 Minutes on Sunday at 8:30pm; CPI and Senate estimates (11:15am) on 28 October; the decision at 2:30pm on 3 November.

cards.headline: US yields little changed after a mixed 20-year auction
cards.takeaway: The auction sold at 5.469% with a larger-than-average tail; CME FedWatch puts the chance of a Fed hike next week at 14.9%.
cards.key_figure: US 10Y 5.13%, +1 bp; US 2Y 4.81%, +2 bp (21 Oct, US Treasury)
cards.new_since_last_issue: The previous issue said the auction was due; the result and the updated FedWatch reading are new.
cards.what_happened: The US Treasury sold US$13 billion of 20-year bonds at a high yield of 5.469%, 0.9 bp above the when-issued level against an average tail of 0.2 bp. Bid-to-cover was 2.73 times against a 2.62 average, while indirect bidders took 58.2% against a 65.2% average ([investingLive](https://investinglive.com/news/us-treasury-sells-13-billion-of-20-year-bonds-at-a-high-yield-of-5-469/)). Markets priced a 14.9% chance of a 25 bp Fed hike on 28 October, down from 33.2% a week earlier and 57.6% a month earlier, according to CME FedWatch, and the 2-year/10-year gap was 31.7 bp ([Reuters via Mint](https://www.livemint.com/market/us-yields-dip-as-ai-risk-weighed-but-move-off-lows-after-auction-11792609214457.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: US long-term yields feed into global borrowing costs, including Australian bond yields. A five-year TIPS auction of US$26 billion follows on Thursday US time.
cards.market_reaction: Dashboard: US 10Y 5.13% (+1 bp) and US 2Y 4.81% (+2 bp), US Treasury par yield curve, 21 Oct.

competing_views.who: Bill Northey, US Bank Wealth Management
competing_views.view: At "5.1% on the 10-year Treasury", bonds provide "competition for flows of capital" from equities.

Moves this small can change sign depending on the time and the measure. The 2-year shows the same pattern (dashboard +2 bp; Reuters +0.2 bp). They should not be averaged.

cards.headline: UK inflation rose to 3.5%, above forecasts, on fuel prices
cards.takeaway: Markets price a 98% chance of a Bank of England hike to 4% next month, according to LSEG data.
cards.what_happened: UK CPI rose 3.5% in the year to September, up from 3.1%, and 0.4% in the month. Core CPI rose to 2.8% from 2.6%, and services inflation to 3.7% from 3.4%. Motor fuels made the largest upward contribution: petrol averaged 169.5 pence a litre and diesel 192.5 pence, the highest since 2022 ([ONS](https://www.ons.gov.uk/economy/inflationandpriceindices/bulletins/consumerpriceinflation/september2026)). Economists polled by Reuters had forecast 3.4%; Westpac's market forecast column had 3.3%. The pound and gilt yields were little changed after the release, and Chancellor John Healey said he would maintain "fiscal discipline" in next week's budget ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/21/inflation-uk-cpi-interest-rates.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: The UK result is another fuel-driven upside surprise in a large energy-importing economy ahead of Australia's September-quarter CPI on 28 October.

competing_views.who: Scott Gardner, J.P. Morgan Personal Investing
competing_views.view: Accelerating services inflation will "create concern that we are starting to see second round inflationary effects beyond energy prices".
"The pieces are falling firmly into place for a November rate rise."

cards.what_to_watch: UK retail sales and flash PMIs on Friday; the Bank of England decision on 5 November.

cards.headline: Iran and the US gave conflicting accounts of tanker mine strikes
cards.takeaway: The IRGC said two tankers hit mines and a third caught fire; CENTCOM said the mine accounts were false. Iranian officials said Iran seeks a deal, and the US added sanctions on shadow-fleet facilitators.
cards.new_since_last_issue: The Close tab reported an IRGC statement about a tanker hitting a mine. New are CENTCOM's response, Wednesday's statements from Araghchi, Pezeshkian, Rezaei and Trump, and the Treasury sanctions.
cards.what_happened: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said on Tuesday that two tankers caught fire after hitting mines on what it called an unauthorised southern route through the Strait of Hormuz, and that a third tanker carrying more than 2 million barrels exploded and caught fire south of the strait; it did not name the vessels ([Xinhua](https://english.news.cn/20261021/0fb02e6579c84b5284058528b71681ee/c.html)). A US Central Command spokesman said Iran's accounts of tankers hitting mines were false: "We have cleared the international waterways in the Strait of Hormuz of mines." The vessels' identities could not be independently confirmed ([IBTimes Australia](https://www.ibtimes.com.au/iran-claims-mines-stopped-tankers-strait-hormuz-1877113)). On Wednesday, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi wrote that Iran "seeks a just and honourable deal" but is "fully prepared to defend ourselves"; President Masoud Pezeshkian said Iran had "submitted our plan to the US"; and security council secretary Mohsen Rezaei said "not a single gram" of enriched uranium will leave Iran. President Trump said, "The last thing I want to do is, upset an apple cart where we're getting close to settling a war" ([Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/live-news/iran-war-news-trump-russia-houthi-october-21), [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2026/10/21/iran-war-live-us-warns-peace-deal-with-tehran-is-extremely-difficult)). The US Treasury sanctioned a Panama- and Greece-based law firm, shipping agents in Singapore and the UAE, and vessels it said support Iran's shadow fleet ([US Treasury](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0664)).
cards.why_it_matters: About a fifth of the world's oil and LNG passes through the strait in peacetime ([IBTimes Australia](https://www.ibtimes.com.au/iran-claims-mines-stopped-tankers-strait-hormuz-1877113)). The International Maritime Organization said it cannot guarantee that a vessel using the traffic separation scheme "will not be hit by a mine" ([Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/live-news/iran-war-news-trump-russia-houthi-october-21)). LSEG analysts said Iran was targeting tankers well beyond the strait, into the Gulf of Oman ([Reuters via Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/oil-rises-middle-east-supply-005041638.html)). Oil prices feed into Australian fuel costs.

cards.headline: France's 10-year yield touched 5% for the first time since 2002
cards.takeaway: The finance minister said the government would use its constitutional power to pass the budget without a vote if needed; Moody's review is due Friday.
cards.new_since_last_issue: The previous issue said yields were just below 5%. On Wednesday they crossed it, the spread over Bunds neared 2011 levels, and the finance minister spoke on the budget.
cards.what_happened: France's 10-year yield touched 5.002% at 9:14 GMT and was last up about 8 bp, just below 5%; its premium over German Bunds was around 157 bp, near levels last seen in 2011 ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/french-10year-bond-yields-hit-5-highest-since-2002-4962104)). Finance Minister Roland Lescure said the government had "guardrails" including Article 49.3, which lets the prime minister pass a bill through the National Assembly without a vote: "If we veer off course, we'll activate the guardrails." Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu is targeting €54 billion of spending cuts; the deficit was 5.1% of GDP last year. Marine Le Pen, described by CNBC as the presidential frontrunner, has said she could bring the deficit below 3% within 18 months of being elected ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/21/france-protests-bonds-debt.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: Government bond yields have risen around the world this year as energy prices pushed central banks to raise rates, and France's borrowing costs have risen more than most peers', according to Reuters. The US 10-year yield is also above 5%.

cards.takeaway: Eight of 11 sectors edged higher, led by industrials and real estate, but falls in energy, materials and consumer discretionary pulled the index lower despite Wall Street's gains.

cards.what_happened: The S&P/ASX 200 fell 34.9 points, or 0.40%, to 8,796.4 (close snapshot, Yahoo Finance). Eight of the 11 sectors rose, although tech was flat: industrials rose 0.9%, real estate 0.8%, telecoms 0.5%, financials and staples 0.4% each, and health care and utilities 0.1% each. Energy fell 2.4%, materials 2.0% and consumer discretionary 1.7% (S&P/ASX 200 sector indices, [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EAXJO/)). Market Index said miners were heading for a third straight session of losses, with BHP and Rio Tinto each down more than 1% at 2pm ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/asx-200-live-today-thursday-22nd-october)).
cards.why_it_matters: Retailers fell after Nick Scali's warning: Wesfarmers closed 3.1%, JB Hi-Fi 1.6% and Harvey Norman 2.9% (Yahoo Finance). Tech was flat even though WiseTech rose 3.1%, after the Nasdaq's 1.1% gain overnight.

cards.headline: Nick Scali falls 15% on profit warning; Fortescue slides on China talks
cards.takeaway: Nick Scali, Magellan and Fortescue fell on company updates and Santos narrowed its production guidance, while NextDC recovered part of Wednesday's fall and Brambles rose on the day of its AGM.
cards.what_happened: **Nick Scali (NCK) −15.3% to A$12.03.** It expects underlying net profit of A$28–32 million for the December half, with Australian and New Zealand written sales orders 15% lower in the first quarter and store traffic about 10% lower; ANZ first-half revenue is expected to be 11–14% below a year earlier, while UK orders rose 29% ([Nick Scali ASX release, 21 Oct](https://www.asx.com.au/markets/trade-our-cash-market/announcements.nck)). Market Index said the A$30 million midpoint is about 20% below the A$37.6 million consensus ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/asx-200-live-today-thursday-22nd-october)). **Fortescue (FMG) −4.5% to A$14.57.** Its full quarterly report confirmed shipments of 46.8 million tonnes and sales of 42.9 million tonnes. It expects product inventory to rise by a further 4–5 million tonnes in October and said that if negotiations with China Mineral Resources Group "are not concluded by calendar year-end, operations may be affected, potentially including adjustments to production"; FY27 guidance is unchanged, subject to those talks ([Fortescue ASX release](https://www.asx.com.au/markets/trade-our-cash-market/announcements.fmg)). **Magellan (MFG) −9.5% to A$7.70.** At its AGM it said financial markets revenue in the September quarter was materially lower than the first-half run rate after sharp moves in bond markets, and assets under management fell 8% to A$38.0 billion ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/asx-200-live-today-thursday-22nd-october), [Magellan ASX release](https://www.asx.com.au/markets/trade-our-cash-market/announcements.mfg)). **Santos (STO) −1.3% to A$9.19.** It reported record quarterly production of 26.3 million barrels of oil equivalent, up almost 14% from the June quarter, and narrowed 2026 production guidance to 99–102 million from 99–105 million ([Santos ASX release](https://www.asx.com.au/markets/trade-our-cash-market/announcements.sto)). Woodside fell 3.5% with no new announcement. **NextDC (NXT) +7.5% to A$5.75**, after falling 42% on Wednesday. **Brambles (BXB) +3.2% to A$21.23**; at its AGM it kept FY27 guidance for sales revenue growth of 2–4% and underlying profit growth of 2–6% at constant currency at its AGM ([Brambles ASX release](https://www.asx.com.au/markets/trade-our-cash-market/announcements.bxb)). Closing prices are from Yahoo Finance.
cards.why_it_matters: Nick Scali's update is an early read on household spending on big-ticket items ahead of the RBA decision. About 90% of Fortescue's iron ore is sold to China ([ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-10-22/asx-markets-business-news-live-updates-thursday-22-october/107295020)), and Wood Mackenzie said China Mineral Resources Group is moving towards shaping how iron ore is priced globally ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/asx-200-live-today-thursday-22nd-october)).

competing_views.view: Kept an Outperform rating with a target price cut 35% to A$12.90, and said NextDC does not need to raise capital.

cards.headline: Brent rises 2% after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia
cards.takeaway: Attacks on the Shaybah oil field and Dammam airport lifted Brent futures, while gold and copper fell.
cards.new_since_last_issue: This morning's briefing covered Brent's flat settlement and the EIA inventory data. The Dammam airport attack and the US departure order are new.
cards.what_happened: At 4:21pm AEDT, Brent futures were at US$111.06 a barrel, up 2.1% from Wednesday's settlement. Gold futures were at US$4,103.4 (−1.1%%) and COMEX copper futures at US$6.481 a pound (−1.0%%) (close snapshot, [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/BZ%3DF/)). The iron ore tile shows US$90.85 a tonne from the latest available print. The Saudi energy ministry said two people were killed when debris from a drone intercepted near a processing plant at Saudi Aramco's Shaybah field hit a contractor's vehicle, and that operations were unaffected. Shaybah produces about 1 million barrels a day. Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said a later attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam killed one person and injured eight; the Houthis had not commented on the airport attack ([The National](https://www.thenationalnews.com/business/energy/2026/10/22/oil-tops-110-as-houthi-drone-strike-near-saudi-shaybah-field-rattles-markets/)). The US State Department ordered non-emergency government employees and their families to leave Saudi Arabia. Spokesperson Tommy Pigott said "Iranian-supported Houthis have increasingly engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure" ([AGBI](https://www.agbi.com/oil-and-gas/2026/10/oil-rises-further-after-dammam-airport-and-oil-field-attacks/), [Reuters via Investing.com](https://au.investing.com/news/commodities-news/oil-rises-as-us-orders-diplomats-to-leave-saudi-arabia-amid-escalating-tensions-4706172)). At the same time, Kuwait Petroleum's chief executive said Kuwait is exporting as much crude as before the war ([ING](https://think.ing.com/articles/the-commodities-feed-oil-supply-risks-outweigh-elevated-oil-flows221026/)).
cards.why_it_matters: Higher oil feeds into the RBA's inflation debate. Energy stocks fell 2.4% today even as crude rose, led by Woodside.

competing_views.view: The risk premium in oil prices "is unlikely to fade until clear signs of de-escalation emerge", even though Persian Gulf flows are holding up.

cards.what_happened: **Saudi Arabia:** whether Houthi attacks on Saudi energy sites and airports continue after the US departure order ([AGBI](https://www.agbi.com/oil-and-gas/2026/10/oil-rises-further-after-dammam-airport-and-oil-field-attacks/)). **Iron ore:** Fortescue's talks with China Mineral Resources Group, with a year-end deadline the company set for possible production changes ([Fortescue ASX release](https://www.asx.com.au/markets/trade-our-cash-market/announcements.fmg)). **CSL:** a class action filed in the Supreme Court of Victoria on behalf of investors who bought CSL securities between 11 February 2025 and 11 May 2026; CSL said it denies liability and will defend it ([CSL ASX release](https://www.asx.com.au/markets/trade-our-cash-market/announcements.csl)). **RBA:** whether the 63% hike pricing holds before next Wednesday's CPI ([RBA Watch](https://rbawatch.com/rba-meeting/november-2026)). **Friday:** Zip, Mineral Resources and Whitehaven Coal quarterlies, Australia's flash PMI and the ABS annual national accounts ([CommSec](https://www.commsec.com.au/content/dam/EN/ResearchNews/2026Reports/October/ECO_Insights_161026-Week-Ahead.pdf)).
cards.why_it_matters: Each could move the ASX open, the rate outlook or oil before the next close.
